Dr. '''Athar Ali''' (20 August 1963 – 4 October 2003) was a Pakistani [[system engineer]] and a [[aerospace engineering|rocket scientist]] who was murdered in [[Karachi]] on 4 October 2003. He was an expert in [[missile|missile technology]] and was the senior scientist at the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission ([[SUPARCO]]) during the time of the development of [[Shaheen (missile)|Shaheen missile guidance system]]. [[SUPARCO]] is a Pakistani governmental agency.  His death led to the mass demonstration in a [[Shiite]] community in Karachi.

==SUPARCO career==
Having joined [[SUPARCO]] in 1985, Ali was associated with the rocket's electrical and electronics system. Thereafter, he specialised in missile technology while the [[Hatf-I|Hatf missile system]] was being developing. At the [[SUPARCO]], Ali was one of the senior scientists involved in the indigenous development of the [[Shaheen-I|Shaheen guidended missile system]]s, and was responsible for the program's electrical and system power engineering at the SUPARCO.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.onlinenews.com.pk/details.php?id%3D39944 |title=ONLINE - International News Network |access-date=2016-07-07 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140503064214/http://www.onlinenews.com.pk/details.php?id=39944 |archive-date=3 May 2014 |df=dmy }}</ref> In 2002, due to his contribution to the agency, he was promoted as the deputy-director of the commission.

==Assassination and culprits==

In the afternoon of 4 October 2003, Ali along with 35 members of [[SUPARCO]] were on the way to [[SUPARCO]] Headquarters. At the 12:45 pm, the [[SUPARCO]] bus dropped some people at a nearby mosque. Three unidentified armed men opened fire.<ref>{{Citation
  | last =Our Staff Reporter
  | title =Six Suparco employees shot dead in city
  | newspaper =[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn News]]
  | date =4 October 2003
  | url =https://www.dawn.com/news/118471/six-suparco-employees-shot-dead-in-city
  }}
</ref>

This [[Drive-by shooting|drive-by-shooting]] lasting just a few minutes, left five dead and eight others wounded including officials of the [[Pakistan Army]] who were on guard duty at the facility. The bodies of the victims were taken to the Murshid Hospital where they were pronounced as dead. Later, the dead bodies were shifted the bodies to the Rizvia Imambargah.<ref>{{Cite news
  | last =Sameer
  | first =Nida
  | title =SUPARCO Scientists targeted and shot dead
  | work = [[GEO News]]
  | date = 4 October 2003}}
</ref>

==Investigation==
According to the online news of Pakistan, the Indian external agency, [[Research and Analysis Wing]] (RAW) has been behind the attacks. The source also concluded that RAW hired activists of [[Quetta]]-based [[Balochistan Liberation Army]] (BLA) outlawed outfit for this incidence of terrorism and real target was Athar Ali who was, in the past, was targeted twice but he was able to manage an escape from the scene.<ref>{{Cite web
 |last=Unknown
 |title=RAW behind SUPARCO bus killings
 |work=Online News
 |publisher=Online News of Pakistan
 |year=2003
 |url=http://www.onlinenews.com.pk/details.php?id=39944
 |url-status=dead
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140503064214/http://www.onlinenews.com.pk/details.php?id=39944
 |archive-date=3 May 2014
 |df=dmy
}}
</ref> The following day of the killings, the FIA had arrested the RAW agent and few other members of BLA. However, [[Government of India|Indian Government]] has denied the allegations and its agency's involvement in the assassinations.<ref>{{Citation
  | last =The Staff Reporter
  | title =Culprits of SUPARCO Bus attack
  | newspaper =Ummat Newspaper
  | language =ur
  | year = 2003
  }}
</ref>

==Aftermath==

Athar Ali's death brought mass demonstration in the [[shiite]] community in Pakistan. The shiite religious parties condemned the death of Dr. Ali, and accused the [[Government of Pakistan]] in the death. The non-profit organisation, [[Imamia Students Organisation]] (ISO), [[Anjuman Tahaffuz Azadari]] (ATA), and [[Tehrik-i-Islami]] (TI) activists on Saturday staged a demonstration to condemn the killings in [[Karachi]]. After the mass demonstration in Karachi, the FIA's special agents arrested the culprits and masterminds of the killings.<ref>{{Cite news
  | title =Coffin of SUPARCO deputy director arrived
  | newspaper =PPI&nbsp;– Pakistan Press International.
  | language =en, ur
  }}</ref> All of the members were closely associated with the [[Sipah-e-Sahaba Pakistan|Sipah-e-Sahab]] and [[Lashkar-e-Jhangvi]]. The associated members were hanged and executed by the Government of Pakistan.<ref name="dawn.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/118471/six-suparco-employees-shot-dead-in-city|title=Six Suparco employees shot dead in city|date=4 October 2003}}</ref>
